title: Working from home (WFH) and weight gain: how to structure your day
intro: WFH makes it easy to gain weight because you take fewer steps and the kitchen is so close. By setting meal times and moving a little throughout the day, you can get back in control.

sections.h: Why weight goes up during WFH
sections.p: When you work at the office, you walk to your car, to the pantry and to places to eat. At home, your steps can drop below 2,000 a day. Add to that snacks that are always right in front of you.
Choose fixed times for breakfast, lunch and afternoon tea. Eat at the dining table, not in front of your laptop. When meals have set times, you nibble less throughout the day.
Walk around the house or in the garden during calls without video. Every hour, get up for 3 to 5 minutes: hang the laundry, take the stairs or stretch. These small steps add up a lot over a day.

Keep biscuits and chips in a cabinet, not on the table. Put fruit, nuts in small containers or yogurt where you can easily see them. If you want kuih, take one and put it on a small plate, don't eat straight from the pack.
When work has no clear end, many people eat dinner late while replying to emails. Set a time to close your laptop. Then go for a 15-minute walk as a sign that the workday is over.

action: Write down your meal times and set phone notifications this week.
Walk every time you have an audio call; aim for 5,000 steps first before going up to 7,000.
Move all sweet snacks into a closed cabinet today.
Prepare your packed lunch the night before, just like when you go to the office.
myth: Many think WFH makes dieting easier because you can cook yourself. In fact, without structure in your day, WFH often makes us eat more often and move less.

faq.q: I always get hungry at 4 pm during WFH. What should I do?
faq.a: Make sure your lunch has enough protein and vegetables. For afternoon tea, try fruit with a handful of nuts or a boiled egg, and teh o with less sugar.

faq.q: No time for the gym. Is walking around the house enough?
faq.a: Walking really helps. It's even better if you add 2 to 3 strength training sessions of 20 minutes at home, using your own body weight like squats and wall push-ups.

faq.q: I work hybrid, sometimes at the office and sometimes at home. How do I stay consistent?
faq.a: Keep the same meal times for both types of days. On WFH days, walk more since you take fewer steps. On office days, bring a packed lunch or plan your meal options before leaving.
